correctness.rationale: For odd p and any K of characteristic p, the ordinary cyclic group algebra is K[T]/((T-1)^p) with augmentation ideal I^p=0. Transport yields u⋆v=alpha(u)beta(v). Augmentation-zero idempotents vanish by iterated ordinary powers of I. Truncated exp/log is a group isomorphism I(+)->(1+I,·), linearizing the augmentation-one idempotent equation to ker(1-alpha-beta). On each regular H=<−1,2> coset in F_p×, Maschke splitting and the only character with chi(-1)+chi(2)=1 show a one-dimensional eigenspace, spanned by explicit V_C. All V_C lie in I and satisfy alpha=-1, beta=2. Thus nonzero idempotents are exactly Exp_p(L), closed under the native quandle law -v+2w, giving count 1+q^r. Rank, explicit construction, operation and complete coefficient enumerations were replayed from the standalone script; they support but do not replace the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The explicit modular classification and quandle law for all odd primes is not stated in the inspected primary published sections. Zhang (arXiv:2610.08204, §2) gives the group-ring transport used as background, but its idempotent classification in §5 is integral/complex, not the modular prime-order census. Elhamdadi–Ta–Virgin (arXiv:2609.03799, §§3–5) prove integral rigidity; Sangare–Ta (arXiv:2608.01550, §§3–4) study characteristic two commutative examples and quandle automorphisms. An indexed mathematical note computes the characteristic-three R_3 idempotent line, which is a known SPECIAL CASE explicitly excluded from novelty. Published and indexed nonmodular finite-field methods require coprime characteristic and do not imply the modular result. Residual risk: unindexed modular classifications or incomplete access to arXiv:2608.09149.
residual_risks: The full relevant calculations of arxiv:2608.09149 were not accessible for direct comparison.

value.rationale: This is a complete algebraic classification in the natural modular characteristic regime excluded by existing coprime-characteristic Fourier counts. It identifies not only an exact finite-field count but the intrinsic quandle structure of every nonzero idempotent and an arithmetic subgroup index controlling its dimension. The first excess p=17 and every p≡1 mod 8 give motivated, infinitely occurring nonbasis-idempotent phenomena; the prior p=3 affine line is subsumed without separate novelty credit.
